messages:
marta-peopleops: Heads up — launching a pilot of the new 'Work From Another Country' (WFAC) policy for short international stays (<=30 days). Effective next Monday.
marta-peopleops: TL;DR: If you plan to be remote from another country for up to 30 days, submit the WFAC pre-approval form, complete a country-risk attestation, and confirm travel/health insurance. Managers should review and approve within 72 hours. People Ops will confirm payroll and benefits handling.

marta-peopleops: Key points:
• Pre-approval form: https://redwood.internal/wfac-request (fill at least 7 business days before travel when possible)
• High-risk/blocked countries: travel to countries on the Restricted list requires additional approval and may be denied.
• Payroll/tax: short stays (<=30 days) generally remain on your current payroll, but if you expect to be gone longer or do frequent multi-country stays, notify payroll.
• Local public holidays: these are NOT automatically applied. If you want to observe local holidays, request PTO as usual or work-through with manager approval.
• Visas & compliance: employees are responsible for visas/entry requirements and any local legal obligations.
• Insurance: purchase the recommended travel health rider; Redwood will provide a vendor discount code.
• Safety: if the country risk rating changes while you're abroad, People Ops will reach out with guidance and next steps.

alex-engineering: Quick Q — I have a 3-week trip to Spain and want to work from there. Do I still accrue PTO and are there any tax implications for me?

marta-peopleops: Good question. PTO accrual continues as normal for <=30 days. For tax/payroll: short stays typically don't change withholding, but it's not universal — if you have income-sourcing questions or will be in-country >30 days in a year, loop in @sam-payroll and @priya-legal for specifics.

sam-payroll: Confirming — for single trips <=30 days we process payroll as usual. If someone crosses 30 days or has repeated visits we may need to change payroll residency. Please flag early so we can advise.

priya-legal: Adding: this is general guidance, not tax/immigration advice. Employees are responsible for visa/entry compliance. We will help with documentation requests for enterprise contractors or special cases.

jamie-engineering: What about Redwood-provided health coverage while I'm in-country? Any support if I need to see a doctor locally?

marta-peopleops: Redwood medical plans may have limited coverage outside your home country. We strongly recommend the travel health rider for trip durations >3 days. EAP and emergency assistance are available 24/7.

alex-engineering: If my manager doesn't respond within 72 hours, what happens?

marta-peopleops: If no manager action within 72 hours we'll send a reminder. If still no response, People Ops will temporarily approve low-risk requests (for <=7 days) so work isn't blocked — managers can still revoke if there are team impacts. Ops will escalate otherwise.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: WFAC request received for alex-engineering (trip: 2026-06-14 to 2026-07-02). Pending manager approval.

sam-payroll: Also — if you expect to be paid in a different currency or by a local entity, submit a ticket to payroll ASAP.

marta-peopleops: Action items: 1) If you're planning to WFAC, fill the form. 2) Managers — please review requests within 72 hours. 3) Anyone with unusual circumstances (visas, tax residency, payroll changes) ping @sam-payroll and @priya-legal.

marta-peopleops: We'll run the pilot for 90 days and iterate based on feedback. Drop questions here or DM People Ops. :wave:
